title: Research method for Alzheimer's disease predicted effector genes (Bellenguez et al., 2022)
bodyHtml:
These results were generated in the study:

New insights into the genetic etiology of Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias.
Bellenguez C, Küçükali F, Jansen IE, Kleineidam L, Moreno-Grau S, Amin S, Naj AC, Campos-Martin R, et al.
Nat Genet. 2022 Apr;54(4):412-436. doi: 10.1038/s41588-022-01024-z.
PMID: 35379992

The authors performed a two-stage genome-wide association study for Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and related dementias (ADD) with 111,326 clinically diagnosed or "proxy" AD cases (reported Alzheimer's disease or dementia in an individual's parent) and 677,663 controls. The GWAS identified 75 risk loci, 42 of which were novel.

At each of these novel loci, protein-coding genes within 1Mb of the lead variant were scored according to seven categories of evidence:

  • variant annotation
  • eQTL (expression QTL)-GWAS integration
  • sQTL (splicing QTL)-GWAS integration
  • pQTL (protein QTL)-GWAS integration
  • mQTL (methylation QTL)-GWAS integration
  • haQTL (histone acetylation QTL)-GWAS integration
  • involvement of the gene in amyloid-β precursor protein (APP) metabolism, as inferred from a genome-wide siRNA screen (Chapuis et al., 2017)

Details of these evidence types and the weights assigned to them are summarized in Supplementary Table 19 of the paper. The sums of these scores are displayed for each gene in the Gene score column. The top score for any gene in the locus is displayed in the Top score column. Individual scores for each of these evidence types are displayed in the Scores row that is visible after clicking the View button for a row in the table.

Next, genes were prioritized in Tier 1 (greater likelihood of being the causal risk gene responsible for the ADD signal) or tier 2 (lower likelihood and the absence of a minimum level of evidence as a causal risk gene) based on a comparison of the gene score and top score, as outlined in Supplementary Figure 34. Genes with weaker evidence were not assigned to tiers.

The table also includes an Expression row that indicates enrichment of gene expression in six brain cell types, as calculated from single-nucleus RNA expression data from the Allen Brain Atlas.
